standard_prerequisites.name: Flat morphisms of ringed topoi and the definition of pullback of modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Modules on Sites, section on flatness (definition of a flat morphism of ringed topoi)
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns exactness of the pullback into the flatness hypothesis.

core_obligations: Show that for an abelian sheaf G on the target the underlying sheaf of sets of f^{-1}G is the inverse image of the underlying sheaf of sets of G, and conclude exactness of f^{-1} on abelian sheaves from the exactness required in the definition of a morphism of topoi (proof lines 5779-5788).

Recall the definition of the pullback of modules as the tensor product with the structure sheaf over f^{-1}O', and use flatness of the morphism of ringed topoi to conclude exactness of f^* (proof lines 5789-5794).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the abelian-sheaf statement to the set-theoretic exactness in the definition of a morphism of topoi.
Reduce the module statement to flatness via the definition of pullback.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves two exactness statements: the inverse image functor on abelian sheaves along any morphism of ringed topoi is exact, and the pullback on modules is exact when the morphism of ringed topoi is flat. The first part uses that the underlying sheaf of sets of the inverse image of an abelian sheaf is the inverse image of the underlying sheaf of sets, so that exactness of the set-theoretic inverse image required in the definition of a morphism of topoi gives exactness on abelian sheaves (proof lines 5779-5788). The second part recalls the definition of the pullback of modules in terms of the structure map and reduces exactness to flatness of the structure map (proof lines 5789-5794). H2: the reduction of the first statement to the definition of a morphism of topoi, and of the second to the definition of flatness, are the substance.
